title: Cloud and Endpoint Security on a Budget
description: Protect local practice servers, learn Defender through Azure Arc, and explore licensed cloud VDI without mistaking a budget for a spending cap.
baseline: lab.example.test · VMware-first free Wazuh path · optional metered/trial Defender for Servers P1 · optional licensed personal AVD · $25 goal, not a guaranteed cap
prerequisite: Let’s build a small security desk you can afford to practise with. Start with your existing VMware machines and free Wazuh. We’ll check Azure costs before turning on Defender, then keep the licensed cloud-desktop exercises clearly optional.
supplies: Your existing VMware host, validly licensed practice Windows Server 2019 APP01, AlmaLinux endpoint and a private management client.
Capacity for the current Wazuh appliance starting point: 4 vCPU, 8 GiB RAM, 50 GB storage. Local hardware/power are not free.
An active Azure subscription, scoped permissions and an accepted plan quote or eligible trial only for Microsoft exercises.
A cost worksheet and cleanup calendar covering Azure usage, fixed licenses, tax and delayed meters. No subscription is created or charged by this website.
A backup and VMware console recovery path; optional VDI requires separate actual AVD/Windows and client-protection entitlements.

steps.title: Separate the three products
steps.where: Your lab notes
actions: Write three lines: Wazuh is free monitoring software; Defender for Endpoint is Microsoft endpoint detection and response; Defender for Cloud includes free posture checks plus separately priced protection plans. Built-in Defender Antivirus is not the same as the paid endpoint portal.

Our low-cost Microsoft route protects a server through Defender for Servers Plan 1 and Azure Arc. It does not require renting Azure VDI, and the server plan does not license Windows 11 client desktops.
Use APP01 as the first server pilot, an AlmaLinux endpoint for Wazuh, and a local Wazuh manager. Keep DC01/DC02 dedicated to directory services.
steps.expected: Your inventory separates local compute, endpoint software and Azure protection.

steps.title: Write a spending stop rule
steps.where: Your worksheet and Azure pricing calculator
actions: The goal is at most $25 per month across services and licenses, not a prepaid package or a guaranteed Azure cap. Inventory existing commitments first.

Price the actual Defender plan/scope, any Azure VM hours, disks, logs, storage and external Microsoft licenses before enabling them. Leave a buffer: for example, stop optional practice at a $10 forecast rather than planning to use every dollar. Rates, billing delay, tax and usage can exceed an estimate.

Start with local VMware/Wazuh and no new cloud VMs. Trials are optional and eligibility is not guaranteed. If no acceptable trial or priced paid plan is available, finish the free lessons and stop before activation.
steps.expected: You have a written estimate, early stop threshold and the choice to continue free.

steps.title: Record names and recovery access
steps.where: VMware and your notes

Do not put a public IP on your practice servers or open inbound RDP to the internet for these exercises. Azure Arc uses outbound service connectivity; it does not move the VM into Azure.

If your subscription must be restored or created, use Microsoft’s billing/signup process and read its offer and payment terms yourself. Do not create subscriptions to evade trial limits, and do not assume an old offer restarts.

steps.title: Protect sign-in and reduce routine privileges
steps.where: Microsoft Entra admin center and Azure Access control (IAM)
actions: Enable or verify MFA using the free Security defaults where appropriate for your practice tenant. Do not change an organization-wide policy in a tenant you do not administer. Conditional Access and Intune have separate license requirements.

Use a scoped onboarding role for Arc and the documented security permissions for Defender configuration. For daily reading, use a reader/security-reader role rather than retaining Owner or Global Administrator for everything.

Cloud sign-in names can initially use your tenant.onmicrosoft.com domain. lab.example.test is a reserved private training name and cannot be verified as a public Entra domain. Keep your tenant’s real .onmicrosoft.com sign-in suffix. Adding a custom domain requires a domain you actually own and a separate verification process; it does not synchronize AD automatically.

steps.title: Tag the resources you can identify
steps.where: Azure portal → lab resource → Tags
actions: Add Environment=Lab, Project=SONIC-Academy, Owner=Learner01 and ExpiresOn with your planned cleanup date. Select Apply/Save. Do not place secrets or sensitive personal data in tags.

Repeat on the individual Arc resources, VMs, disks and workspaces you create. Resource-group tags are not automatically inherited by resource objects; a deliberately configured policy can copy them. Cost Management tag inheritance affects reporting and is a separate feature.
ExpiresOn is a reminder until you build and verify automation that reads it. Start VM on Connect and autoscale also require actual configuration and permissions.
steps.expected: The actual lab resources carry useful, non-secret tags.

steps.title: Create a budget and early alerts
steps.where: Azure portal → Cost Management + Billing → Cost Management → Budgets
actions: Select the exact subscription scope. Choose Add/Create budget, name CloudSeam-Security-Lab, set a monthly reset and amount 25 in your billing currency. If that is not USD, adjust the amount to your real spending goal.
Set actual-cost alerts at 40%, 60% and 80%, plus a forecast alert where your offer supports it. Enter your own monitored email or approved action group and save. Test that notifications reach you.

A budget is an alert, not a hard spending cap or guaranteed shutdown. Cost data and alerts can be delayed, and external Microsoft 365 subscriptions may be billed separately. Do not wait for a final $25 alert before acting.

steps.title: Explain where the savings come from
steps.where: Azure portal → Cost Management → Cost analysis
actions: Filter or group costs by Project/Environment and check individual resources. Some meters do not support tags; check the untagged entries as well.

Imagine an old disk tagged Owner=Learner01 and ExpiresOn last week. The tag makes it findable; confirming it is unused and deleting it is what removes future storage charges. Record saved result before deleting anything.

Use this estimate: total = fixed licenses + compute rate × active hours + protection charges + disks/storage/logs/network. A hypothetical $0.10/hour VM costs $4 for 40 hours versus $73 for 730 hours, before all other charges. That is arithmetic, not an Azure quote.
steps.expected: You can identify a cost owner and the real stop/delete action behind a saving.

steps.title: Create one harmless file-integrity event
steps.where: APP01 Wazuh agent configuration and private dashboard
actions: Create C:\SecurityLab. Back up the Wazuh agent configuration and add that directory to the existing syscheck configuration using Wazuh’s linked Windows FIM instructions; do not duplicate the full syscheck block. Use realtime monitoring where supported.

Restart only the Wazuh agent after validating configuration, wait for its starting point and change a harmless text file in that directory using the command below. No executable or malware is involved.
Find the resulting event in Wazuh. Record agent, path, time and action; a missing event is a collection/configuration problem to investigate, not permission to mark the exercise passed.
steps.command:
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\SecurityLab
Set-Content -LiteralPath C:\SecurityLab\practice.txt -Value "CloudSeam harmless practice change"
steps.expected: The file change produces a matching event for APP01.

Read the current pricing and trial status before any Save. If an eligible trial is offered, record the actual start/end and a reminder several days before expiry. actions: Verify device isolation is supported for this OS/agent and your plan, and that your role permits it. Open the VMware console first. Use a practice member-server pilot, never DC01, DC02 or the monitoring manager.

If the action is available and approved for this lab, choose Isolate device, add the practice reason and confirm. Expect ordinary guest connectivity and its web application to be disrupted while the Defender control channel is maintained where supported.

steps.title: Turn the plan Off in the portal
steps.where: Azure portal → Defender for Cloud → Environment settings → lab subscription
actions: Find Servers and choose Off. Follow Continue if shown, then Save. Reopen the page and confirm the saved setting. Keep the free Foundational CSPM layer if you want it; do not confuse it with the paid Defender CSPM switch.

Check resource-level overrides, relevant Policy assignments/remediations and any legacy workspace-level Plan 2 settings. Turning off the subscription plan does not necessarily remove a per-resource override or a policy that enables it again.
Review every other paid Defender plan you enabled. This is a dedicated practice environment: removing protection from a business server needs a separate approved replacement plan.

steps.title: Offboard intentionally and preserve basic protection
steps.where: Defender portal, Azure Arc machine and local console
actions: Follow current Microsoft offboarding guidance for the actual onboarding method and portal experience. Verify whether automatic offboarding applies; do not assume a saved Off switch instantly removes installed agents or every tenant association.

If retiring the lab connection, use the documented Arc disconnect procedure on the correct server after reviewing its extensions and required connections and services, then reconcile the cloud resource. Do not just delete a portal record and assume the local agent or protection is gone.
Keep required local Antivirus/firewall active, and keep Wazuh if that is your continuing monitoring path. Historical portal records may remain; verify actual sensor state and billing separately.

actions: For Azure VMs created in optional exercises, use Stop/Deallocate in Azure and verify Stopped (deallocated); a guest shutdown can remain billed. For Arc, connected-state server metering and delayed heartbeats follow the current billing rules; do not infer zero costs from closing the console.

Delete only practice resources after checking backups/dependencies. Check resource-group contents individually; deleting this group does not cancel subscription-wide plans, tenant-wide onboarding or external Microsoft 365 subscriptions. Stop recurring licenses/trials through their own billing pages before their conversion/renewal date if not continuing.
Review costs again after usage records settle and check the next invoice. Record what remains enabled, what can still charge and any unresolved meter; budget alerts can lag and are not a hard cap.

steps.title: Separate VDI from the free VMware lab
steps.where: Your planning worksheet
actions: A remote desktop in VMware teaches administration but is not Azure Virtual Desktop. AVD includes host pools, application groups, workspaces, user license or evaluation permission and Azure session-host infrastructure.

This optional branch uses one personal Windows 11 Enterprise single-session host and one assigned learner, not several always-on desktops or a multi-session fleet. Avoid managed AD DS, VPN Gateway and FSLogix shared profile storage in this first Entra-joined personal-host exercise.
The free local starting point remains available if the licensed cloud design does not fit. Do not relabel a server’s two administrative RDP sessions as a licensed user VDI service.

steps.title: Check the actual entitlement and trial terms

actions: Review Microsoft’s current eligible AVD licenses for each user and the matching Windows/hosting rights. Verify your actual assigned subscription, qualifying OS requirements and expiry with the license terms. A Defender-only user license does not provide Windows or AVD rights.

Business Premium is an example of an eligible bundle, not a mandatory purchase. An eligible trial can be evaluated only under its actual terms. Annual advertised prices are commitments, not a one-month lab price, and cloud resources may still bill during a license trial.

Verify a supported CLIENT endpoint protection license or evaluation permission for the Windows 11 host. Defender for Servers Plan 1 covers server OSs; it does not turn that client host into a covered server. Do not use external-user AVD pricing as a workaround for your own internal lab identity.

steps.title: Create the host pool basics
steps.where: Azure portal → Azure Virtual Desktop → Host pools → Create
actions: Before the wizard, open Azure Subscriptions → your lab subscription → Resource providers. Check Microsoft.DesktopVirtualization. If it is NotRegistered, have the authorized setup operator select Register and wait for Registered; registration needs the documented subscription permission. Do not give the daily reader account Owner just to skip this check.
Select the approved subscription and a separate practice VDI resource group. Enter a clear host pool name such as hp-cloudseam-personal-lab and an allowed region.

Choose Personal rather than Pooled. Use automatic personal assignment for this one learner, or an explicitly documented direct-assignment method. Keep this a small lab/validation pool if the wizard offers that setting.
Read the final cost/entitlement gate again before you add a billable VM. The wizard labels can change; use the linked deployment guide for your current portal.

actions: Choose Add virtual machines = Yes, count = 1, a clear name prefix and the approved region. Record the actual generated VM name; do not assume the prefix is the complete hostname.

Select a supported Windows 11 Enterprise single-session image and a currently supported x64 VM size adequate for Windows and the security agent. Review the actual hourly rate and disk tier; do not choose a tiny unsupported size just because its number is lower.

Confirm the eligible Windows license declaration only if the learner really has the required rights. Do not select a costly marketplace software image, extra data disks or availability infrastructure without repricing.

actions: Use the practice lab VNet/subnet with required outbound AVD/Entra/Microsoft service connectivity. Do not assign a public IP to the session host or open internet-facing 3389. AVD’s supported reverse-connect access is not the same as exposing RDP directly.

Choose Microsoft Entra ID join for this first exercise and confirm the required sign-in extension/deployment options in the current wizard. Use your tenant’s generated .onmicrosoft.com learner identity. Do not try to verify the fictional lab.example.test name in Entra. Do not try to create another AD forest with the same name.

Leave Intune enrollment off unless its license or evaluation permission and enrollment design were explicitly included. This exercise does not require renting Entra Domain Services or connecting your home AD through a paid VPN gateway.
steps.expected: The host has a supported identity/network design without public RDP or surprise identity services.

actions: Create or select the lab workspace and register the desktop application group. Record the actual workspace and application-group names.
Review all fields, image, count, region, identity, tags and estimated charges. Choose Create only after that review and the earlier cost/license gate; otherwise cancel.
Wait for deployment completion and check the session-host status in the host pool. Fix deployment/agent errors rather than repeatedly creating more VMs.

steps.title: Assign the learner and test sign-in
steps.where: AVD application group → Assignments; VM Access control (IAM)
actions: Assign the intended Entra learner to the desktop application group using the supported Desktop Virtualization User assignment. For an Entra-joined host, grant the required Virtual Machine User Login permission at the appropriate narrow scope; admin sign-in is a different role.

If using direct personal assignment, assign that specific session host to the learner. Use a supported Windows App or AVD web client to subscribe/sign in to the workspace with the licensed learner identity.

Confirm the desktop starts without opening public 3389. If it fails, check application-group assignment, VM login permissions, identity, MFA/session requirements and session-host health. Do not fix it by making every learner an administrator.

actions: Record OS/build, assigned user, VM/disk names, private network, sign-in method and actual running state. Confirm a tested way to manage/recover the host before security experiments.

Onboard client EDR only with the exact supported client license/plan and current VDI guidance for this persistent personal host. Do not use the server Arc/Plan 1 exercise as a substitute for that license.

Keep this first host persistent. Non-persistent multi-session images need a separate image/VDI onboarding design to avoid duplicate identities and inherited enrollment secrets. Add that only after this personal-host starting point works.

lessons.title: Secure and Stop the Cloud Desktop
lessons.description: Verify client protection, configure controlled uptime and clean up at the end of the trial.
lessons.what: Optional licensed VDI extension. Let’s verify client protection, configure controlled uptime and clean up at the end of the trial.
lessons.why: Cloud VDI adds identity, user access, image and lifecycle controls—and its licenses do not stop billing when you log out.
needs: A working optional personal desktop with supported client protection license or evaluation permission
Recovery access and current AVD scaling permissions
bestPractices: Use only your isolated CloudSeam practice machines. Record scope, a recovery method and the expected result before changing anything.
Protect secrets and use fake learner/ticket data in screenshots. Never upload onboarding secrets or passwords to the Academy.
A checkbox records your notes. It does not prove that a security sensor is healthy or that billing stopped.
commonMistakes: Treating a $25 budget or an ExpiresOn tag as an automatic spending cap.
Turning on every paid plan or a whole production subscription to protect one test server.
Confusing a discovered device with a healthy onboarded endpoint.

troubleshooting.problem: The portal or result differs from the picture.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the selected tenant, subscription, resource and current official source. Record the exact message. Stop at a scope, license, billing or health mismatch instead of enabling more services.

lessons.pass: Show supported protection, observed deallocation behavior and a complete resource/license end-of-trial record.

quiz.question: Does deallocating a desktop cancel its monthly user license?
options: No; license billing is a separate lifecycle
Yes, immediately
Only when it is tagged ExpiresOn
quiz.explanation: No; license billing is a separate lifecycle is the intended practice for this class.

steps.title: Pilot client protection without locking out the learner
steps.where: Client security portal and the assigned desktop
actions: Verify this host’s actual client EDR onboarding and recent reporting, using the supported licensed product’s current steps. Use a vendor-approved safe test and record its actual result. Server and client portals/features can differ.

Apply one pilot policy through a licensed/supported management channel. Test sign-in, desktop launch and necessary applications. If using Conditional Access or Intune, confirm the needed licenses and a tested administrator recovery account before enforcement.

Do not isolate the only remote session host as your first response exercise without a separate supported recovery path. The earlier containment practice belongs on the VMware member-server console pilot.
steps.expected: Client protection is verified without accidentally removing all recovery access.

steps.title: Start only when needed and deallocate after use
steps.where: Azure Virtual Desktop → scaling plan/host pool settings
actions: Review the supported personal-host scaling-plan guide. Configure a limited practice schedule and the required service-principal RBAC scope; a schedule without permissions cannot stop the host.

Enable Start VM on Connect where appropriate for your host-pool design and verify its permissions. Test signing out, deallocation and a later connection that starts the host. It is not a universal timer and user sessions can affect scale-down.

Until tested automation works, manually Stop/Deallocate the actual VM in Azure after saving work and signing out. Verify Stopped (deallocated). Guest shutdown/disconnect is not enough, and disk and license costs can continue.
steps.expected: You observe the real power transition and know which remaining meters still charge.

steps.title: End the extension before renewal surprises
steps.where: Azure inventory, Cost Management and the separate license billing portal
actions: Export only approved sanitized learning evidence. Before trial expiry, decide whether to buy/renew the actual user and client licenses; disable recurring billing/cancel through the provider’s process if not continuing. Do not assume deleting a VM cancels a license.

Remove the practice VDI host, disks, workspace/application group/host pool and any extra resources only after confirming nothing shared depends on them. Recheck for orphan disks, snapshots, diagnostic workspaces and other meters.

Review delayed usage and the next invoice, update the inventory and keep the local free practice path if the ongoing licensed cloud cost exceeds the goal. Record that this optional VDI environment was retired rather than pretending it remains protected.
steps.expected: The extension has a verified end state for both Azure resources and separate licenses.
